floor_history.headline: Recon confirmed: honest floor 2 (83/83 insns); sole residual is a 2-insn sched2 tie in the prologue cluster (sll $3,$18,4 vs the $16 save/copy). No rules, no cheat-asm.
s2 structural: 3 more hypotheses killed (guard-form neutral, s5-hoist and operand-swap harmful); sched2 tie still 2-insn residual, no C-structural lever hand-derived so far.

frontier.hypothesis: Instrumented cc1 -da RTL dump on current candidate.c reveals the exact INSN_PRIORITY of the sll pseudo vs the move16 pseudo in sched2 and the pivot downstream chain member (currently believed: sll->addu $1->lw $20->addu $21 = length 4 vs move16->slt->beqz = length 3). Confirming which insn's chain terminator dominates lets us target the C for exactly that dependence.
frontier.mechanism: sched.c INSN_PRIORITY = length of longest downstream data-dependence chain within the basic block; ties broken by insn UID (creation order). The chain terminator identity tells us which downstream insn to relocate/shorten in C.
frontier.next_probe: Preprocess text1a_c.c to base.i via cc1 -E path; run `tools/gcc-2.7.2/build/cc1 <build-flags> -da base.i` in tmp/grind/func_80045294/s3/; parse the .sched2 dump for func_80045294 and extract priorities for prologue-region insns. Cross-reference sched2 tiebreak logic to confirm the mechanism.

frontier.hypothesis: Expressing the loop iterator differently (e.g. `for (i = a0; i < count; i++)` with the initializer inside for's init-clause) rearranges tree_LUID and RTL creation order enough to change the sched2 tiebreaker without disturbing the RA fingerprint.
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2 expands `for`-init as the FIRST statement of the loop nest; this can steer pseudo creation order for i differently than a bare `s32 i = a0;` declaration.
frontier.next_probe: Rewrite the guard+loop as `for (i = a0; i < count; i++) { ... }` (moving i's init into the for-clause) while keeping v1-before-i by declaring v1/s4 first. Sandbox. If it moves the tie, expand to other init-clause placements.

frontier.hypothesis: Permuter campaign with a CLEAN single-function target.o (base score = weighted diff without ~340k branch-address noise) will find a directed-PERM prologue-region spelling that hand-probes missed.
frontier.mechanism: Random + PERM_* directed mutations of guard/loop/init spellings across 20-30 fresh seeds — the cross-product of forms is far larger than hand-probes can cover.
frontier.next_probe: Build target.o from asm/funcs/func_80045294.s + decomp-permuter prelude (per tmp/grind/func_80045294/s1/diff_target.sh scaffolding). Run permuter --stop-on-zero on candidate.c; monitor for closing forms and cheat-vet each before proposing.
